html:
The movement of farming and pottery making people from the lower Orinoco River in what is now Venezuela into the islands of the Caribbean, beginning around 500 BCE. They are named after the site of Saladero on the Orinoco.

The Saladoid people paddled canoes up the chain of the Lesser Antilles and reached Puerto Rico. They brought farming of cassava (manioc), village life and fine white on red painted pottery. Earlier, the islands had been home to hunter-gatherers who had come by sea long before.

Saladoid villages lasted for about a thousand years. Their descendants and later arrivals developed the cultures that the Spanish met in 1492: the Taíno of the Greater Antilles, the people Columbus first encountered. The migration was one of the great sea crossings of the ancient Americas.
sum: The movement of farming and pottery making people from the lower Orinoco River in what is now Venezuela into the islands of the Caribbean, beginning around 500 BCE. They are named after the site of Saladero on the Orinoco.
